questions.prompt: A change makes the loop send one extra request after the text reply. The script has 2 replies. What happens in the test?
options: The mock repeats the last reply, so the test passes
The third request throws script exhausted, so the test fails
The real model answers the third request
The loop skips the extra request
questions.explanation: Each request takes the next entry. With 2 entries, a third request finds the script empty and throws, which shows the loop asked once too often.

questions.prompt: Why does the test keep the real tools and the real record, and fake only the model?
options: The model is the only part that is costly and changes its answers, so faking only it still tests the shipped code
The record needs a real model
questions.explanation: The model costs money and answers differently each time. Everything after it is cheap and repeatable, so keeping it real proves that the real code works.

questions.prompt: What does assert on mock.requests[1] check?
options: That the mock's text is correct
That the model counted the lines
That the loop sent the tool result for call_1 in its second request
questions.explanation: The mock records each request it gets. Checking the second request shows that the loop added the right tool result, which is the loop's job.
